structure.caption: Figure 3: FY2025 Annual Financial Overview

spec.title: FY2025 Annual Financial Overview
spec.subtitle: Fiscal Year Ended 31 December 2025 | Apex Industrial Technologies, Inc.

sections.heading: Executive Summary
sections.body: Apex Industrial Technologies delivered resilient performance in FY2025, achieving full-year revenue of $4.82 billion, up 6.4% compared to FY2024. Growth was driven by disciplined pricing actions, an improved product mix, and sustained demand in mission-critical automation solutions. Operating margin expanded 140 basis points year over year to 18.7%, reflecting productivity gains and cost optimization initiatives executed throughout the year.

sections.heading: Revenue and Profitability
sections.body: Gross profit increased to $1.96 billion, representing a gross margin of 40.7%, compared to 38.9% in the prior year. Selling, general, and administrative expenses were tightly managed at 15.2% of revenue, down 60 basis points year over year. Operating income rose to $902 million, while net income attributable to shareholders reached $624 million. Diluted earnings per share increased 11% to $3.48, supported by higher operating leverage and a modest reduction in weighted average shares outstanding.

sections.heading: Segment Performance
sections.body: The Industrial Automation segment reported revenue of $2.95 billion, an increase of 4%, driven by retrofit and aftermarket activity in North America and EMEA. The Software & Services segment grew 12% to $1.31 billion, benefiting from higher recurring subscription revenue and expanded analytics offerings, with segment margins exceeding 26%. The Engineered Components segment experienced flat revenue at $560 million due to softer OEM demand in the second half, though pricing discipline mitigated margin pressure.

sections.heading: Cash Flow and Capital Allocation
sections.body: Operating cash flow totaled $713 million, up 9% year over year, reflecting improved working capital management and earnings growth. Capital expenditures were $214 million, primarily directed toward digital infrastructure and capacity upgrades in the Midwest manufacturing facilities. The company returned $180 million to shareholders through dividends and repurchased $95 million of common stock under its existing authorization.

sections.heading: Outlook for FY2026
sections.body: For FY2026, Apex expects revenue growth in the range of 3% to 5%, assuming moderating industrial demand and stable input costs. Operating margin is projected between 18.5% and 19.0%, supported by continued mix shift toward higher-margin Software & Services offerings. Diluted earnings per share are anticipated to range from $3.65 to $3.85. Management remains focused on pricing discipline, selective investments in innovation, and prudent cost management to sustain earnings growth.

structure.full_text:
FY2025 Annual Financial Overview
Fiscal Year Ended 31 December 2025 | Apex Industrial Technologies, Inc.

Section Executive Summary
Apex Industrial Technologies delivered resilient performance in FY2025, achieving full-year revenue of $4.82 billion, up 6.4% compared to FY2024. Growth was driven by disciplined pricing actions, an improved product mix, and sustained demand in mission-critical automation solutions. Operating margin expanded 140 basis points year over year to 18.7%, reflecting productivity gains and cost optimization initiatives executed throughout the year.

Section Revenue and Profitability
Gross profit increased to $1.96 billion, representing a gross margin of 40.7%, compared to 38.9% in the prior year. Selling, general, and administrative expenses were tightly managed at 15.2% of revenue, down 60 basis points year over year. Operating income rose to $902 million, while net income attributable to shareholders reached $624 million. Diluted earnings per share increased 11% to $3.48, supported by higher operating leverage and a modest reduction in weighted average shares outstanding.

Section Segment Performance
The Industrial Automation segment reported revenue of $2.95 billion, an increase of 4%, driven by retrofit and aftermarket activity in North America and EMEA. The Software & Services segment grew 12% to $1.31 billion, benefiting from higher recurring subscription revenue and expanded analytics offerings, with segment margins exceeding 26%. The Engineered Components segment experienced flat revenue at $560 million due to softer OEM demand in the second half, though pricing discipline mitigated margin pressure.

Section Cash Flow and Capital Allocation
Operating cash flow totaled $713 million, up 9% year over year, reflecting improved working capital management and earnings growth. Capital expenditures were $214 million, primarily directed toward digital infrastructure and capacity upgrades in the Midwest manufacturing facilities. The company returned $180 million to shareholders through dividends and repurchased $95 million of common stock under its existing authorization.

Section Outlook for FY2026
For FY2026, Apex expects revenue growth in the range of 3% to 5%, assuming moderating industrial demand and stable input costs. Operating margin is projected between 18.5% and 19.0%, supported by continued mix shift toward higher-margin Software & Services offerings. Diluted earnings per share are anticipated to range from $3.65 to $3.85. Management remains focused on pricing discipline, selective investments in innovation, and prudent cost management to sustain earnings growth.

spec.title: Apex Industrial Technologies — FY2025 Annual Performance Summary
spec.subtitle: For the Fiscal Year Ended 31 December 2025 | Investor Briefing Extract

sections.heading: Overview of Financial Performance
sections.body: Apex Industrial Technologies reported FY2025 revenue of $4.82 billion, an increase of 7.4% compared to $4.49 billion in FY2024. Growth was driven by disciplined pricing actions across the Industrial Systems portfolio and a continued shift toward higher-margin Software & Services offerings. Operating income rose 14% year over year to $812 million, reflecting both volume leverage and targeted cost optimization initiatives implemented in the second half. Diluted earnings per share increased to $3.96 from $3.28 in the prior year.

sections.heading: Margin Expansion and Cost Actions
sections.body: Adjusted operating margin expanded 120 basis points to 16.8%, primarily due to favorable mix and productivity gains within manufacturing operations. The company executed approximately $55 million in annualized cost reductions through procurement savings, footprint rationalization, and selective workforce realignment. Gross margin improved to 38.5%, supported by pricing discipline that offset residual raw material volatility. Management maintained strict capital allocation controls while preserving investment in growth initiatives.

sections.heading: Segment Performance
sections.body: Industrial Systems generated revenue of $3.05 billion, up 4%, with steady demand in energy infrastructure and specialty components partially offset by softer order intake in general manufacturing late in the year. The Software & Services segment delivered 15% growth to $1.77 billion, with recurring subscription revenue now representing 62% of segment sales. Segment operating margin in Software & Services reached 24.3%, reflecting scale benefits and a richer mix of cloud-based analytics solutions. Backlog entering FY2026 stood at $2.1 billion, providing moderate visibility into the first half.

sections.heading: Cash Flow and Capital Deployment
sections.body: Operating cash flow totaled $690 million, compared with $603 million in FY2024, driven by improved earnings and disciplined working capital management. Free cash flow conversion was 92% of net income, enabling the company to reduce net debt by $180 million. Apex repurchased $125 million of common shares and increased its quarterly dividend by 8% in October 2025. Capital expenditures of $210 million were directed toward automation upgrades and expansion of the digital services platform.

sections.heading: FY2026 Outlook
sections.body: For FY2026, management expects revenue growth of 3% to 5%, reflecting moderating demand conditions in certain cyclical end markets. Adjusted operating margin is projected between 17.0% and 17.5%, supported by continued mix shift and incremental productivity gains. Diluted earnings per share are anticipated in the range of $4.20 to $4.40, assuming stable foreign exchange rates and no material changes in input costs. structure.full_text:
Apex Industrial Technologies — FY2025 Annual Performance Summary
For the Fiscal Year Ended 31 December 2025 | Investor Briefing Extract

Section Overview of Financial Performance
Apex Industrial Technologies reported FY2025 revenue of $4.82 billion, an increase of 7.4% compared to $4.49 billion in FY2024. Growth was driven by disciplined pricing actions across the Industrial Systems portfolio and a continued shift toward higher-margin Software & Services offerings. Operating income rose 14% year over year to $812 million, reflecting both volume leverage and targeted cost optimization initiatives implemented in the second half. Diluted earnings per share increased to $3.96 from $3.28 in the prior year.

Section Margin Expansion and Cost Actions
Adjusted operating margin expanded 120 basis points to 16.8%, primarily due to favorable mix and productivity gains within manufacturing operations. The company executed approximately $55 million in annualized cost reductions through procurement savings, footprint rationalization, and selective workforce realignment. Gross margin improved to 38.5%, supported by pricing discipline that offset residual raw material volatility. Management maintained strict capital allocation controls while preserving investment in growth initiatives.

Section Segment Performance
Industrial Systems generated revenue of $3.05 billion, up 4%, with steady demand in energy infrastructure and specialty components partially offset by softer order intake in general manufacturing late in the year. The Software & Services segment delivered 15% growth to $1.77 billion, with recurring subscription revenue now representing 62% of segment sales. Segment operating margin in Software & Services reached 24.3%, reflecting scale benefits and a richer mix of cloud-based analytics solutions. Backlog entering FY2026 stood at $2.1 billion, providing moderate visibility into the first half.

Section Cash Flow and Capital Deployment
Operating cash flow totaled $690 million, compared with $603 million in FY2024, driven by improved earnings and disciplined working capital management. Free cash flow conversion was 92% of net income, enabling the company to reduce net debt by $180 million. Apex repurchased $125 million of common shares and increased its quarterly dividend by 8% in October 2025. Capital expenditures of $210 million were directed toward automation upgrades and expansion of the digital services platform.

Section FY2026 Outlook
For FY2026, management expects revenue growth of 3% to 5%, reflecting moderating demand conditions in certain cyclical end markets. Adjusted operating margin is projected between 17.0% and 17.5%, supported by continued mix shift and incremental productivity gains. Diluted earnings per share are anticipated in the range of $4.20 to $4.40, assuming stable foreign exchange rates and no material changes in input costs. The company remains focused on disciplined pricing, recurring revenue expansion, and prudent cost management to sustain earnings growth.

structure.full_text:
Apex Industrial Technologies — FY2025 Annual Performance Summary
For the Fiscal Year Ended 31 December 2025 | Issued: 18 February 2026

Section Executive Overview
Apex Industrial Technologies delivered resilient growth in FY2025, achieving consolidated revenue of $8.74 billion, an increase of 6.8% over FY2024. Growth was driven by disciplined pricing actions across Industrial Systems and a higher contribution from recurring Software & Services revenue. Adjusted operating income rose 140 basis points to 18.6%, reflecting structural cost initiatives and improved product mix. Management maintained focus on cash generation, resulting in free cash flow of $1.12 billion, up 9% year over year.

Section Revenue and Margin Performance
Gross margin expanded to 34.9%, compared to 33.1% in the prior year, supported by supply chain efficiencies and selective repricing in response to input cost normalization. Adjusted earnings per diluted share increased to $3.42 from $3.05 in FY2024, representing 12% growth. GAAP net income totaled $786 million. The Company reduced SG&A as a percentage of revenue by 60 basis points through targeted overhead rationalization and shared services consolidation.

Section Segment Results
Industrial Systems generated revenue of $5.26 billion, up 4.1%, with operating margin improving to 17.2% on stronger aftermarket demand and productivity gains. Software & Services revenue grew 14.5% to $2.18 billion, benefiting from higher subscription renewals and new cloud-based analytics deployments; segment margin reached 25.8%. The Engineered Components segment reported $1.30 billion in revenue, flat year over year, as moderating capital spending in EMEA offset strength in North America. Across segments, recurring revenue accounted for 38% of total company sales, compared to 34% in FY2024.

Section Capital Allocation and Balance Sheet
At year-end, net debt stood at $2.05 billion, with a net leverage ratio of 1.6x EBITDA, reflecting disciplined capital deployment. The Company returned $420 million to shareholders through dividends and share repurchases during the year. Capital expenditures totaled $310 million, focused on automation upgrades and digital platform enhancements. Apex maintained investment-grade credit metrics and ended the year with $1.4 billion in available liquidity.

Section FY2026 Outlook
For FY2026, management expects revenue growth in the range of 3% to 5%, reflecting moderating industrial demand in Asia-Pacific and stable order backlogs in North America. Adjusted operating margin is projected between 18.8% and 19.3%, supported by continued mix shift toward Software & Services and incremental cost savings of approximately $85 million. Adjusted EPS is anticipated to range from $3.55 to $3.75. The Company remains committed to balanced capital allocation while prioritizing investments that enhance recurring revenue and long-term shareholder value.
